page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.16xlarge is an instance in the High Clock Speed family, provisioned via KVM virtualization. The instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 256.0 GB, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core, which balances computing capacity against volatile memory requirements.

The platform does not include hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs, and contains no local storage volumes. Storage must be provisioned externally using remote block storage solutions. For network connectivity, the instance offers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses, accommodating consistent traffic throughput between cluster nodes and attached storage systems.

Because the server combines a high 3.1 GHz core clock speed with a balanced memory allocation, it serves computational workloads requiring fast clock cycles alongside standard RAM densities. Architectural tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and absence of specialized vector or matrix hardware flags. The configuration is suitable for enterprise application servers, batch processing, build pipelines, relational databases relying on networked storage, and data processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.16xlarge is a high clock speed virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with x86_64 architecture at 3.1 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory to maintain a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and features no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for operating systems and persistence. Network performance is anchored by a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its combination of elevated CPU clock speeds and standardized general-purpose memory density, the instance accommodates compute-bound applications, scalable backend application servers, continuous integration pipelines, batch operations, and networked database workloads.
